fact: For finite real D>0, if x∈[0,∞] satisfies x≥s+1 for every real 0<s<D, then x≥D+1.
justification: This expands the packet's explicit order argument. For any real q<D+1 set m=max(0,q−1) and s=(D+m)/2. Both 0≤m<D and m<s<D follow from D>0 and q−1<D. Thus 0<s<D and q<s+1. If x=∞ the conclusion is immediate. If x is finite and x<D+1, take q to be its real representative; the displayed s gives x<s+1, contradicting the given bound. No continuity or convergence theorem is required, and no finiteness of x is assumed. This is routine ordered-field completion of the exact route already stated.
